put.description:
Replace the library's paths and tag rules; every version is then re-processed.

Send the whole set (`GET /libraries/{owner}/{repo}` has the current `settings`): what is
left out is cleared. Changed paths queue a `reprocess` job that fetches every version
again at the commit it serves (a branch is not synced) and re-imports it; only tag rules
changed queue a `retag` job that re-tags the stored articles, fetching nothing. Each
version keeps serving its old state until its new one is complete, then switches at
once (after a `retag`, search's tag filters follow the listings a moment later); one
that fails keeps the old state and the job fails naming it. Sending the same settings
again re-runs that failed job. Answers 202 with the job in `Location`, or 200 with no
job when the settings are unchanged and the last re-processing did not fail (or there
is no version yet: imports to come use them). 422 for an invalid pattern or tag (nothing
is stored), 404 for an unknown library.

post.description:
Re-sync the library's branch versions: import the ones whose tip moved.

Only changed articles are re-chunked. Commits are never checked and tags never moved:
a tag that still names its commit is `pinned`. Read each version's `status`, not the HTTP
status, for what happened to it: `up_to_date`, `queued`, `importing` (an import of it is
already queued or running), `failed` with an `error_code`: `ref_deleted` (the branch or
tag is gone upstream), `tag_moved` (the tag names another commit now; it is reported,
and re-imported only when confirmed with `versions/reimport`) or `unexpected` (its
import could not be queued). Every version keeps what it served. Queued imports answer
202, anything else 200. 409 `version_importing` when a running import left nothing
queued. 422 when the remote cannot be read, mostly `repo_unreachable` (deleted, private,
moved or down; also a login prompt for a library without a credential) or `auth_failed`
(the credential was refused or cannot be read).
Other codes are possible: `host_key_changed` (the SSH host key changed, possibly a man
in the middle) and `git_not_installed`; any 422 means nothing was fetched. The failed
jobs recorded for it are named in the message.

put.description:
Check the library on its own every `interval_minutes`, starting at the next tick.

Each check asks the repository for its refs once. Tags matching `tag_pattern` that have
a version order (`v1.4.0`, `2.1`; pre-releases do not) are imported as `auto` versions,
oldest first, and only the newest `keep_last` `auto` versions are kept: older ones are
removed once their replacements are versions. Versions added by hand (`manual`) and the
pinned default are never removed and do not count. A tag whose import failed for good
(`no_articles`, `import_too_large`) is tried again only once it moves; after repeated
`unexpected` failures it backs off (doubling, at most a day); other failures are tried at
the next check. An `auto` version removed by hand comes back
while it is among the newest `keep_last`. With `sync_branches`, every branch version is
re-synced as `POST .../sync` would. Send the whole set: what is left out takes its

The manual tags of a path as stored: every version's article at that path carries them.

So does, in a later version, the article git saw it renamed to.

TokenGrant.title: TokenGrant
TokenGrant.description: A new token. ``token`` is the only copy of the secret and is never shown again.

TokenSummary.title: TokenSummary
TokenSummary.description: A token as listed: everything but the secret.

reprocess.description: `paths`: the selection changed, every version is fetched again at its commit; `tags`: only tag rules changed, every version is re-tagged from what is stored; null: nothing changed and nothing is re-run, nothing is re-processed.

job_id.title: Job Id
job_id.description: The job re-processing every version (`/jobs/{id}`); one already queued for the library is reused. Unchanged settings re-run the library's last re-processing job when it failed. Null when nothing is to do or the library has no versions yet.

versions.title: Versions
versions.description: The library's refs now, at the commits they serve: what the job re-processes (it reads the versions again when it runs). Listed also when a queued job is reused.

UpdatedLibrarySettings.title: UpdatedLibrarySettings
UpdatedLibrarySettings.description: The settings as stored (normalized) and the job that brings every version in line.

is_default.title: Is Default
is_default.description: True for the version `/owner/repo` resolves to.

origin.description: `auto` when the library's scheduled check imported it (retention may remove it), `manual` when someone added it.

VersionOut.title: VersionOut
VersionOut.description: One imported version: the ref, what kind of ref it is, and the commit it stands for.

exactdocs__catalog__models__RefKind.title: RefKind
exactdocs__catalog__models__RefKind.description: What a version was imported from.

exactdocs__catalog__models__TagMatch.title: TagMatch
exactdocs__catalog__models__TagMatch.description: Whether an article needs any or all of the filter's tags.

exactdocs__catalog__models__VersionOrigi.title: VersionOrigin
exactdocs__catalog__models__VersionOrigi.description: Who asked for a version: a person, or the scheduled check (which may prune its own).

exactdocs__ingestion__models__RefKind.title: RefKind
exactdocs__ingestion__models__RefKind.description: What a requested ref turned out to be.

exactdocs__ingestion__models__VersionOri.title: VersionOrigin
exactdocs__ingestion__models__VersionOri.description:
Who asked for a version: a person (``manual``) or the scheduled check (``auto``).

Retention (``AutoSync.keep_last``) only ever removes ``auto`` versions.

exactdocs__retrieval__models__TagMatch.description: How a tag filter combines its tags.
